options: Converting data into a format that is accessible, usable, readable and actionable
Reducing the number of rows in a query result
Replacing real data with synthetic values
Isolating data so only one team can see it
questions.explanation: Data Standardisation means converting data into such a format that it is accessible, usable, readable and actionable.

questions.stem: At which two levels can Data Standardisation be imposed?
options: Data level and data store level
questions.explanation: Data Standardisation can be imposed at a data level or at a data store level.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as an effect of Data Standardisation?
options: Increases the number of data silos
questions.explanation: Standardisation reduces manual effort, removes duplication, enforces governance and enables segmentation; it works against silos rather than increasing them.

questions.stem: What is the first of the listed steps for Data Standardisation?
options: Know your data and what it is required for
Standardise your data with the help of data scoring
questions.explanation: The steps begin with knowing your data and what it is required for, then recognising entry points, outlining standards and standardising with data scoring.

questions.stem: Which technique is named in the final step of Data Standardisation?
questions.explanation: The last listed step is to standardise your data with the help of data scoring.

questions.stem: Which example illustrates a Data Standardisation approach for semi-structured data?
options: Converting all dates into a single format
Translating data from different languages into English
Exposing data as reports and dashboards
Converting JSON and XML into one readable format
questions.explanation: Converting multiple semi-structured formats such as JSON and XML into one readable format is a listed standardisation approach.

questions.stem: Which Data Standardisation approach relies on an MDM system?
options: Data pipeline processing at one given time
Converting video and audio into a readable format
Converting dates into a single format
questions.explanation: Having Gold Records using an MDM system is one of the standardisation approaches.

questions.stem: Which of these is listed as a benefit of Data Standardisation?
questions.explanation: Better Data Lineage is among the benefits, along with a single source of truth, easier data quality, access management, reusability and easier catalogue and metadata management.

questions.stem: What do the 'quality gates' created during Data Standardisation indicate?
questions.explanation: Enriching metadata and creating quality gates that indicate freshness and anomaly is a listed standardisation approach.

questions.stem: Into which structures can data from all relevant source systems be brought as a Data Standardisation approach?
options: A Unified Data Model in a Data Warehouse, a Star or Snowflake schema, a Semantic Layer or a multi-dimensional Cube
questions.explanation: One approach brings data from all relevant sources into one Unified Data Model in a Data Warehouse, Star or Snowflake schema, Semantic Layer or multi-dimensional Cube.
